original_question: Is it relatively consistent with ZFC that there exists a separable Banach space X for which the partially ordered set K(B_X) of weakly compact subsets of the closed unit ball B_X, ordered by inclusion, is not Tukey equivalent to any of the four standard types {0}, N^N, K(Q), or the family of finite subsets of the continuum?
target_in_paper: Problem 1.6 in §1.2 (Compactness in Banach spaces): Is it relatively consistent that there is a separable Banach space X such that K(B_X) is not Tukey equivalent to {0}, N^N, K(Q), or the family of all finite subsets of c?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual open problem. It has the right metamathematical form (relative consistency with ZFC), the right class of spaces (separable Banach spaces), the right ordered object K(B_X) (weakly compact subsets of the closed unit ball ordered by inclusion), and the right four benchmark Tukey types. It also correctly follows the paper's four-type Banach-space list rather than Fremlin's broader five-type list, so it properly omits N.
missing_details: The paper works throughout with real Banach spaces, so the ambient scalar field should be made explicit for a fully paper-faithful stand-alone statement.
For stand-alone clarity, B_X should be explicitly defined as the closed unit ball {x in X : ||x|| <= 1}.
For stand-alone clarity, K(B_X) should be explicitly defined as the poset of all weakly compact subsets of B_X, ordered by inclusion.
It should be explicit that Tukey equivalence is being taken between partially ordered sets.
The fourth benchmark type is best given in the paper's standard notation as [c]^{<ω}, i.e. the family of all finite subsets of a set of cardinality c, ordered by inclusion.
If one wants the statement to mirror the nearby context precisely, K(Q) should be identified as the poset of compact subsets of the rationals ordered by inclusion.
refined_question: Is it relatively consistent with ZFC that there exists a real separable Banach space X such that, if B_X denotes the closed unit ball of X and K(B_X) denotes the partially ordered set of all weakly compact subsets of B_X ordered by inclusion, then K(B_X) is not Tukey equivalent to any of the four posets {0}, N^N, K(Q), or [c]^{<ω}, where K(Q) is the family of compact subsets of Q and [c]^{<ω} is the family of all finite subsets of a set of cardinality c, each ordered by inclusion?
justification: The draft is essentially Problem 1.6 itself. The surrounding paragraph explains exactly why these four comparison types are the relevant ones: the authors note that, under analytic determinacy, K(B_X) is Tukey equivalent to one of {0}, N^N, K(Q), or [c]^{<ω}, and that this classification is already provable in ZFC when X does not contain l1. The refined version therefore keeps the scope exactly as in Problem 1.6 and only adds the paper's standing convention that Banach spaces are real plus explicit definitions of the benchmark posets and notation so the question is fully self-contained.
